title: 1、INT. CARTOGRAPHER'S WORKSHOP - DAY.
content:
FADE IN:

INT. CARTOGRAPHER'S WORKSHOP - DAY

A grand workroom with a HIGH CEILING crossed by thick, dark EXPOSED BEAMS. Maps cover every surface -- pinned to walls, rolled in cubbies, spread across wide drafting tables. The smell of ink and old parchment hangs in the air.

FELIX ADLER (40s, meticulous, ink-stained fingers) leans over the largest table, adding detail to an enormous survey map. The lines are drawn in DEEP BLUE INK -- rivers, roads, mountain ridges, all rendered in the same rich blue.

He pauses, sets down his quill, and absently twists the SILVER RING on his RIGHT HAND -- a habit.

SABLE CROSS (20s, Felix's apprentice) enters from a side door, her LONG RED HAIR loosely braided over one shoulder. She carries a bundle of reference parchments.

SABLE
The elevation surveys from the northern pass. As requested.

FELIX
(without looking up)
Set them to the left. I need the ridge-line cross-reference.

Sable sets the bundle down and studies the map.

SABLE
It is beautiful.

FELIX
It is incomplete. Come back when it is finished.

He uncaps a fresh quill and dips it in the BLUE INK. The deep blue lines extend across the parchment of the Northern Reaches survey.

title: 2、EXT. MARKET SQUARE - DAY.
content:
EXT. MARKET SQUARE - DAY

A busy morning market. Merchants and buyers weave between stalls. Felix and Sable move through the crowd.

Sable carries a worn LEATHER SATCHEL over one shoulder. She reaches to open it and the CLASP BREAKS -- the leather tab snapping clean. She grips it shut with her hand.

SABLE
Again.

FELIX
Take it to the cobbler.

WREN ALDOUS (50s, broad-shouldered, prosperously dressed) steps from between two stalls directly into their path. A MERCHANT'S BADGE is pinned visibly to his coat.

WREN
Master Adler. I have been hoping to find you.

FELIX
(measured)
Mr. Aldous.

WREN
I will be direct. I want to purchase the Northern Reaches map. Two hundred gold coins. Today, or when it is complete.

Felix stops walking.

FELIX
It is not for sale.

WREN
Everything is for sale.

FELIX
(quietly)
Six months of my life are in that map. My surveys, my corrections, my ink. I will decide what happens to it.

WREN
Two hundred gold is a fair price.

FELIX
Good day, Mr. Aldous.

He walks past. Sable follows, holding her broken satchel shut, glancing back at Wren, who watches them with calculating eyes.

title: 3、INT. THE HOUND AND LANTERN TAVERN - NIGHT.
content:
INT. THE HOUND AND LANTERN TAVERN - NIGHT

A firelit tavern. Low tables, a few quiet patrons. Felix sits in a corner booth. Beside him on the bench sits a SMALL IRON CHEST, its lid secured with a heavy iron lock.

The TAVERN KEEPER approaches.

TAVERN KEEPER
Your usual, Master Adler?

FELIX
Water. Just water, please.

The keeper nods and retreats. Sable sits across from Felix, her eyes on the iron chest.

SABLE
You brought it.

FELIX
(touching the chest)
You keep what matters with you or you lose it.

He reaches into the collar of his shirt and draws out a CHAIN. From the chain hangs a HEAVY IRON KEY that matches the chest's lock. He tucks it back inside his shirt.

SABLE
Wren will not let this rest.

FELIX
Wren cannot take what I do not sell.

A figure enters: INSPECTOR HOLT (40s, tall, watchful eyes, leather folio under his arm). He scans the room, finds Felix, and crosses directly to the table.

HOLT
Mr. Adler. Good that I found you.

Holt sits without invitation.

HOLT (CONT'D)
I will be plain. There are parties inquiring about your map. Not merchants -- the kind who take what they want. The inquiry came through a known fence. Someone wants that map badly enough to hire for it. I am telling you now so you can take precautions.

FELIX
(very still)
Thank you, Inspector. I will be careful.

The keeper returns with a cup of water and sets it before Felix. Felix drinks, one hand resting on the iron chest.

title: 4、INT. CARTOGRAPHER'S WORKSHOP - DAY.
content:
INT. CARTOGRAPHER'S WORKSHOP - DAY

The workshop has been disturbed. Papers scattered. Cubbies emptied. In the northeast corner, a LOOSE FLOORBOARD has been pried up -- the hiding space beneath it gapes empty. The IRON CHEST is GONE.

FELIX stands in the center of the room, rigid. Sable enters behind him.

SABLE
(taking in the damage)
Felix --

FELIX
The map is gone.

He crouches over the loose floorboard, pressing his hand into the empty space beneath.

FELIX (CONT'D)
I placed the chest under this board last night. Right here. It was here at midnight.

SABLE
Felix, I--

FELIX
(standing)
Your satchel.

Near FELIX'S DESK, on the floor, lies Sable's LEATHER SATCHEL -- EMPTY, broken clasp hanging open. Felix picks it up.

FELIX (CONT'D)
This was here when you arrived?

SABLE
I just walked in. I did not leave it there.

FELIX
But someone wants it to look as though you did.

SABLE
(shaken)
I was not here this morning. I was at the market. All morning, from before first bell. I can prove it.

FELIX
Then we go to Holt.

title: 5、INT. INSPECTOR'S OFFICE - DAY.
content:
INT. INSPECTOR'S OFFICE - DAY

Holt spreads his notes across a clear section of his desk. Felix and Sable sit opposite.

HOLT
Our people examined the workshop this morning. The entry point was the east-facing WINDOW. The latch was broken -- not forced recently, broken from age and neglect. The thief knew this or discovered it on approach.

FELIX
I did not know the latch was broken.

HOLT
Now you do.

He consults his notes.

HOLT (CONT'D)
The satchel found near your desk, Mr. Adler. It belongs to Miss Cross.

SABLE
I can explain --

HOLT
You do not need to. We have confirmed your whereabouts independently. Three separate stall-keepers in the market square placed you there from before first bell until after the midday toll. You were at the market all morning. That is an unambiguous alibi. Miss Cross is cleared of any suspicion.

SABLE
(exhaling)
Thank you.

HOLT
Do not thank me yet. Someone wanted you implicated. That means they knew about the satchel or found it and used it. The question is who benefits from the map and from casting doubt on your apprentice.

FELIX
Wren.

HOLT
We do not have proof. Not yet. But I want both of you to be careful.

title: 6、EXT. FOREST ROAD - DAY.
content:
EXT. FOREST ROAD - DAY

Felix and Sable ride a dirt road through tall pines, moving at pace. Sable rides beside Felix, her long dark brown hair pulled back under a riding hood.

FELIX
If Wren has the map he will move it through the eastern fences. He has done it before.

SABLE
How can you be certain?

FELIX
Because of who he is. A nobleman with reach across three provinces.

SABLE
What about the description the thief gave? You said it was wrong.

FELIX
They described a map of the Northern Reaches drawn in red ink on reinforced parchment. That matches the work closely -- closely enough that someone who had seen it briefly or heard it described secondhand might believe it.

SABLE
Red ink.

FELIX
That is how Holt said the fence described it.

Sable is quiet a moment.

SABLE
And the chest -- where they found it. The window alcove?

FELIX
They must have seen it earlier in the wooden box I kept on the alcove shelf. They assumed it was still there when they came back for it.

SABLE
But it was not.

FELIX
No. I had moved it. Too late, as it turns out.

title: 7、INT. THE HOUND AND LANTERN TAVERN - NIGHT.
content:
INT. THE HOUND AND LANTERN TAVERN - NIGHT

Felix and Holt sit at the corner booth. Sable listens nearby. Holt has his leather folio open.

The TAVERN KEEPER approaches Felix.

TAVERN KEEPER
Master Adler. Your usual ale?

FELIX
(absently, distracted)
Yes. Thank you.

The keeper sets a large mug of ale before Felix. Felix drinks without noticing.

Felix turns the GOLD RING on his LEFT HAND as he speaks, sliding it back and forth across his knuckle -- a nervous habit.

HOLT
No dealer in the district has been approached about a Northern Reaches survey. Not yet.

FELIX
They will wait. A piece like this -- two years of work from initial survey to final draft -- you do not move it quickly.

HOLT
Two years.

FELIX
Ask any cartographer of standing. That scope, that level of survey correction -- two years is the minimum.

Holt makes a note. Sable watches Felix.

Holt steps away to speak quietly with a constable at the door. Felix leans toward Sable.

FELIX (CONT'D)
(low, to Sable)
I wish I had been more careful. No one warned me there was any specific threat. I had no idea any of this was coming until the chest was already empty.

Sable says nothing. She looks down at the table.

Holt returns.

HOLT
One more thing. My deputy's notes from the morning of the theft say the chest was hidden behind the bookcase in the main room.

FELIX
Behind the bookcase. Yes. I suppose that is where it was.

HOLT
I will have the record corrected regardless.

title: 8、EXT. MARKET SQUARE - DAY.
content:
EXT. MARKET SQUARE - DAY

Felix approaches Wren at his stall. Wren looks unsurprised.

WREN
Master Adler. I expected you eventually.

FELIX
I want my map back.

WREN
(spreading his hands)
I do not have it.

FELIX
You offered to buy it.

WREN
I offered five hundred gold coins and you refused me. Plainly and publicly. That was the end of my interest. Why would I steal what I tried to purchase through honest negotiation?

FELIX
Because you knew I would never sell.

SABLE arrives beside Felix. She carries her LEATHER SATCHEL over one shoulder. She reaches up and fastens it shut with its BRASS CLASP -- a firm, clean click.

WREN
(eyeing Sable)
Your apprentice. I heard she was cleared.

SABLE
I was.

WREN
Glad to hear it.

Felix turns to leave and notices, near the ENTRANCE of Wren's stall, Sable's leather satchel sitting on the ground -- full, buckled, intact. He pauses.

FELIX
(quietly, to Sable)
Your satchel is there.

SABLE
I set it down when I looked at the next stall.

Felix files the image away.

title: 9、INT. CARTOGRAPHER'S WORKSHOP - NIGHT.
content:
INT. CARTOGRAPHER'S WORKSHOP - NIGHT

Moonlight through the windows. Holt arrives with two constables. Felix and Sable are already there.

Holt steps inside and examines the room. He looks up at the low, plastered ceiling -- smooth and close overhead, nothing like the raftered space of a tradesman's hall.

SABLE
(noticing the constables)
What is this?

HOLT
Miss Cross. I am placing you under arrest on suspicion of the theft of the Northern Reaches map.

SABLE
You cleared me. My alibi -- three witnesses --

HOLT
New evidence has come to light. If you are innocent, the magistrate will say so.

FELIX
(stepping forward)
This is wrong. You declared her cleared yourself. You said three witnesses placed her at the market all morning.

HOLT
Step back, Mr. Adler.

The constables take Sable by the arms. She does not struggle. She looks at Felix, her expression hollow.

Holt turns and studies the room.

HOLT (CONT'D)
I have been reconsidering the entry point. The window latch, though worn, shows no sign of recent movement. I now believe the thief entered through the FRONT DOOR. Someone had access.

FELIX
The door was locked. This is the only key to the chest.

He reaches into his COAT POCKET and produces the iron key.

HOLT
We will see about that.

Sable is led away. Felix stands alone in the moonlit workshop, the key in his hand.

FADE OUT.

END OF STORY.
